html:
Mount Mugh is a castle site in the upper Zeravshan valley of Tajikistan where Devashtich, ruler of Panjakent, made his last stand against the Arab armies in 722.

Devashtich claimed the throne of Sogdia and joined a revolt against the Umayyad conquest. Besieged on the mountain, he surrendered and was executed. Sogdia was then slowly brought into the Muslim world, and within two centuries its people spoke Persian, under the Samanids.

In 1932 a shepherd found a basket of documents in the ruins. Most are in Sogdian, written on leather, paper and sticks: letters, contracts and accounts of Devashtich's court. With the Ancient Letters they are the main written source for daily life in Sogdia, and helped scholars decipher the language.
sum: Mount Mugh is a castle site in the upper Zeravshan valley of Tajikistan where Devashtich, ruler of Panjakent, made his last stand against the Arab armies in 722.
